answer: Behavioral Divergence Audit. Each identity must periodically answer a randomly seeded challenge whose correct response depends on its accumulated private history. Clones share identical histories, so their answers collide; genuine agents diverge like grain in basalt. Enforcement flags any collision cluster, freezing all members. To evade, an attacker must run and maintain genuinely distinct histories per identity, paying separate compute, storage, and orchestration costs—timber and harbor fees scale linearly with clone count, erasing the sybil advantage.
